newsitem.title: UK: UK building chiefs warn on stg threat to recovery.
newsitem.headline: UK building chiefs warn on stg threat to recovery.

text.p: UK building chiefs warned on Tuesday that if sterling remained at its current heady levels it could start to hit the industry by early next year.

Sir Martin Laing, president of the Construction Confederation and chairman of John Laing Plc, told a press briefing "The strength of sterling will have an effect on the industry by early next year. It is hurting exporters and UK manufacturing. If we did start to see redundancies as a result, it could have an effect on consumer confidence and the housing market."
Laing made the comments after announcing its latest survey which showed the construction industry had increased output for the fifth successive quarter in the second quarter of 1997.
The pace of growth had slowed, but the Construction Confederation said recovery was still on track. Sterling could be one factor which could hamper this rebound, however.

The current consumer spending boom was only being controlled by interest rate rises which was adding to the pain of British industry, said Laing. In the past such spending was funded by borrowing so rate hikes could dampen demand.
But the building society windfall payments bonanza made the problem difficult to tackle, he said.
The construction industry feared that once companies started to shed jobs as a result of sterling's strength, the housing market recovery could falter.

"We've had the euphoria of the new Labour government. But this situation with sterling is the first major area in which the government has to do something. It's bigger than anything else," said Laing.
